- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.9 to 0.1), adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day mean, not extreme peaks or troughs.  
- Avoid forecasting spikes beyond 2 standard deviations above recent 18-day mean — especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If forecast shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the following 3–5 periods’ forecast by 5–10% to account for momentum decay.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, use a weighted average of recent 7–10 day mean and 18-day mean to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
